title: Reconnecting to internet after downtime triggers flood of notifications from apps that remained open during that time
line: When an app sends a burst of notifications, it now shows at most four popups and a summary like "146 more notifications from FloodTest" instead of cycling through every one for minutes.
explanation: Every incoming notification became a popup. When an app sent a burst (a chat app catching up after resume or reconnecting), the popup model just queued them and showed as many as fit (five on an 800 px screen), each for the full timeout, so 150 messages kept the right side of the screen busy for two to three minutes. Nothing detected bursts; the only summary was the Do Not Disturb one. Now the popup model checks, whenever a popup is added, how many popups each app has waiting: above five it keeps the oldest four, marks the rest expired like the Do Not Disturb summary does (they stay in the history) and shows one "N more notifications from <app>" popup with Show Notifications, updating its count while the burst goes on.

commits.message:
notifications: summarize bursts of popups from one application

When an app sent many notifications at once, e.g. a chat app catching up
after resume, all of them popped up for minutes. Now an app shows at
most four popups, the rest only go to the history behind a summary.

BUG: 441906

media.caption: Master, 150 notifications from one app: 0, 5 and 10 s later it is still cycling through them five at a time (messages 1-5, 6-10, 11-15); this goes on for about 2.5 minutes
With the fix, same flood: four popups plus "146 more notifications from FloodTest" at 0 s, only the summary at 5 s, nothing left at 10 s
Master, right after the flood: a stack of five FloodTest popups that keeps being replaced
With the fix: the first four messages and a summary popup with Show Notifications
Master: the flood as a video (20 s of it)
With the fix: the same flood as a video
